parts.label: main

parts.reason: P3.3 covers conversion between Cartesian and parametric forms explicitly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Partial fractions decomposition
parts.reason: P2.10 covers decomposing rational functions into partial fractions with linear factors, matching this denominator form.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Integration using partial fractions and logs
parts.reason: P8.6 explicitly covers integrating using partial fractions linear in denominator, giving ln results.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Vector subtraction to find a vector between points
parts.reason: P10.3/P10.4 cover vector addition/subtraction and position vectors; finding RQ from PQ and PR is a standard application.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Scalar (dot) product to find angle between vectors
parts.reason: No P10 statement explicitly mentions the scalar/dot product or the formula a.b=|a||b|cosθ for finding angles between vectors; P10.5 is vague ('use vectors to solve problems') and doesn't name this method explicitly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Binomial expansion for rational/negative index (a+bx)^n
parts.reason: P4.1 explicitly extends binomial expansion to any rational n.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Range of validity of binomial expansion
parts.reason: P4.1 explicitly requires awareness that expansion is valid for |bx/a|<1.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Using expansion for numerical approximation
parts.reason: P4.1 guidance explicitly mentions use for approximation.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Volume of revolution by integration
parts.reason: No statement in the list mentions volumes of revolution; P8.3 only covers area under a curve/between curves, not rotation about an axis. This concept is absent from the given spec statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Parametric differentiation to find tangent
parts.reason: P7.5 explicitly covers differentiating parametrically and finding tangents to parametric curves.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding domain endpoint from parametric curve
parts.reason: Uses parametric equations understanding (P3.3) and evaluating endpoint values; standard application within domain/range work of P2.8/P3.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding range of a function from parametric curve
parts.reason: Range of functions is covered under P2.8 (domain and range of functions) applied to this parametric curve.

parts.label: i
parts.technique: Integration by substitution
parts.reason: P8.5 explicitly covers integration by substitution including finding a suitable substitution.

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: Integration by parts (repeated application)
parts.reason: P8.5 explicitly allows integration by parts with more than one application of the method.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Proof by contradiction
parts.reason: P1.1 explicitly lists proof by contradiction as a required method, applicable to unfamiliar proofs like this factorisation-based argument.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Vector equations of lines in 3D and proving lines are skew
parts.reason: None of the P10 statements mention vector equations of lines (r = a + λb form) or the concept of skew lines; they cover points, magnitude, addition and position vectors only, not line equations or line-line relationships.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Setting up and solving a differential equation with separable variables (rate proportional to inverse square)
parts.reason: P7.6 covers constructing differential equations in context; P8.7 covers solving separable first order differential equations with given information to find constants.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Using solution of differential equation to find a specific time
parts.reason: P8.8 covers interpreting the solution of a differential equation in context.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Sketching solution curve of differential equation
parts.reason: P8.7 guidance explicitly mentions sketching members of family of solution curves; P8.8 covers interpreting solutions in context including validity, consistent with sketching the graph.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Implicit differentiation
parts.reason: P7.5 explicitly covers differentiating functions and relations defined implicitly for the first derivative.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Using implicit differentiation result to find stationary points (turning points north/south)
parts.reason: Builds directly on the in-spec result from part (a) (dy/dx=0 condition), applying standard stationary point technique (P7.3) to an implicit curve; the underlying method (implicit differentiation, P7.5) is in spec so this is a valid continuation.
